title: To make technical corrections to the Guam World War II Loyalty Recognition Act.
sponsor: Del. San Nicolas, Michael F. Q. [D-GU-At Large]
official_summary: This bill modifies the use of amounts deposited in the Guam World War II Claims Fund, which is used to pay claims of victims and survivors of the attack and occupation of Guam by Imperial Japanese military forces and the liberation of Guam by U.S. military forces. Currently, claims are paid subject to the availability of appropriations. This bill removes the requirement for appropriations.

summary.headline: This law removes a requirement that claims from the Guam World War II Claims Fund wait for separate congressional appropriations before being paid.
summary.what_it_does: The Guam World War II Claims Fund pays claims from victims and survivors of the Japanese occupation of Guam and the U.S. liberation of Guam. Before this law, those claims were paid only if Congress provided appropriations for them. This law removes that appropriations requirement, so the fund's deposited amounts are used to pay claims directly.

who_it_affects.group: Victims and survivors of the Japanese attack and occupation of Guam during World War II
who_it_affects.how: Their approved claims are paid from the Guam World War II Claims Fund without depending on a separate appropriation from Congress.

who_it_affects.group: Congress and federal agencies that administer the claims fund
who_it_affects.how: They no longer need a yearly appropriation to make claims payments from the fund.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on March 26, 2020; the official summary does not state a separate effective date.
